version.changelog: Initial release — governed agent email setup (sandbox-by-default, human-in-the-loop escalation).

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed sandbox email-integration helper with human approval gates for production or external sending.

dimensions.detail: The requested capabilities fit the stated purpose: provisioning a sandbox inbox, generating a reviewed policy, scaffolding governed send/read code, running sandbox self-tests, and requesting human approval for promotion.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad for agent email requests, but the runtime instructions keep actions scoped to Mailbuttons email setup, require policy confirmation, and repeatedly prohibit external send, production promotion, scope widening, and bypassing quarantine.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact consists of markdown instructions and references only, with no executable scripts or hidden installer; it declares curl and a sandbox MAILBUTTONS_API_KEY environment variable.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Email access and API-key use are sensitive but proportionate to creating an agent inbox, and the artifacts direct tokens to stay in environment variables and generated code to avoid hard-coded secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The only persistent changes described are expected project files such as mailbuttons.policy.json and scaffolded integration code; production promotion and external sending require a separate human approval flow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want an agent email inbox through Mailbuttons. Use a sandbox token, review the generated policy before continuing, and keep production promotion or external sending as a deliberate human-approved step.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger phrases are email-specific and aligned with the skill purpose; this is worth user awareness but is mitigated by sandbox-only instructions and explicit confirmation before continuing.
[suspicious.exposed_secret_literal] unexpected: The flagged line contains an API endpoint and placeholder token names, not a hard-coded secret; the artifact repeatedly tells agents not to hard-code keys.
